AN ORDINANCE AMENDING THE LAND USE ORDINANCE OF WARREN COUNTY, GEORGIA, RELATING TO MANUFACTURE, STORAGE, APPLICATION OR OTHER USE OF SOIL AMENDMENTS; AMENDING SECTIONS 2 (DEFINITIONS AND INTERPRETATIONS), 4

(LAND USE DISTRICTS), 5 (REGULATIONS FOR SPECIFIC LAND USES), AND 9 (ADMINISTRATION AND ENFORCEMENT) OF THE LAND USE ORDINANCE; AND FOR OTHER PURPOSES

WHEREAS, the Warren County Land Use Ordinance (the "Ordinance”) was originally enacted on January 10, 2006; and

WHEREAS, the Warren County Board of Commissioners (the “Board"), as governing authority for Warren County, has determined that there is a need to amend and modify certain provisions of the Ordinance to address certain issues as a result of experience; and

WHEREAS, notice of Intent to amend the Ordinance has been accomplished in accordance with the procedures of the Ordinance and the Georgia Zoning Procedures Law, O.C.G.A. § 36-66-1 et. seq.; and

WHEREAS, the Planning Commission has considered this matter and determined that the Ordinance should be amended in accordance with the provisions contained in the Articles below;

NOW, THEREFORE BE IT ORDAINED by the Board that the following amendments shall be made to the Land Use Ordinance of the Code of Warren County, Georgla:

Land Use Ordinance of the Code of Warren County Georgla, Is hereby amended to add the following definitions as follows:

Aaricultural area: This term shall have the same meaning as set forth in O.C.G.A. § 41-1- 7(b){1), as may be amended from time to time.

As of its inclusion in this Ordinance, “agricultural area” means any land which is, or may be, legally used for an agricultural operation under applicable zoning laws, rules, and regulations at the time of commencement of the agricultural operation of the agricultural facility at issue and throughout the first year of operation of such agricultural facility.

Agricultural facility: This term shall have the same meaning as set forth in O.C.G.A. § 41-1- 7(b)(2), as may be amended from time to time.:

As of its inclusion in this Ordinance, “agricultural facility” means any facility including, but not limited to, any land, building, structure, pond, impoundment, appurtenance, machinery, or equipment which is used for the commercial production or processing of crops, livestock, animals, poultry, honeybees, honeybee products, livestock products, poultry products, timber, forest products, or products which are used in commercial aquaculture. Such term shall also include any farm labor camp or facilities for migrant farm workers.

Aaricultural operation: This term shall have the same meaning as set forth in O.C.G.A. § 41-1- 7(b)(4), as may be amended from time to time.:

As of its inclusion in this Ordinance, “agricultural operation” shall include any of the following activities. (A) The plowing, tilling, or preparation of soil at an agricultural facility; (B) The planting, growing, fertilizing, harvesting, or otherwise maintaining of crops as defined in O.C.G.A. § 1-3-3 and also timber and trees that are grown for purposes other than for harvest and for sale; (C) The application of pesticides, herbicides, or other chemicals, compounds, or substances to crops, weeds, or soil in connection with the production of crops, timber, livestock, animals, or poultry; (D) The breeding, hatching, raising, producing, feeding, keeping, slaughtering, or processing of livestock, hogs, equines, chickens, turkeys, poultry or other fowl normally raised for food, mules, cattle, sheep, goats, dogs, rabbits, or similar farm animals for commercial purposes;

(E) The production and keeping of honeybees, the production of honeybee products, and honeybee processing facilities;

(F) The production, processing, or packaging of eggs or egg products; (G) The manufacturing of feed for poultry or livestock;

(H) The rotation of crops, including without limitation timber production; (1) Commercial aquaculture;

(J) The application of existing, changed, or new technology, practices, processes, or procedures to any agricultural operation; and

(K) The operation of any roadside market.

Industrial by-product: This term shall have the same meaning as set forth in Ga Comp. R. & Regs. 40-31-1-.01(10), as may be amended from time to time.:

As of its inclusion in this Ordinance, “industrial by-product” means any industrial waste which is capable of beneficial use, reuse, or recycling as a soil-amendment.

Industrial waste: This term shall have the same meaning as set forth in Ga Comp. R. & Regs. 40-31-1-.01(11), as may be amended from time to time.:

As of its inclusion in this Ordinance, “industrial waste” means any discarded material generated through industrial, commercial, mining, manufacturing, or agricultural operations. Industrial waste includes solid, liquid, semisolid, contained gaseous material, or a combination thereof. Industrial waste does not include un-manipulated manure or sewage sludge.

Sewage sludge: This term shall have the same meaning as set forth in Ga. Comp. R. & Regs. 391-3-6-.17, as may be amended from time to time.

As of its inclusion in this Ordinance, "sewage sludge” means: solid, semi-solid, or liquid residue generated during the treatment of domestic sewage or a combination of domestic sewage and industrial wastewater in a treatment works. Sewage sludge includes, but is not limited to, scum or solids removed in primary, secondary, or advanced wastewater treatment processes. Sewage sludge does not include ash generated during the firing of sewage sludge incinerator, grit and screenings generated during preliminary treatment of domestic sewage in a treatment works, treated effluent, or materials excluded from definition of “sewage sludge” by O.C.G.A. § 12-5-30-.3(a)(1).

Sludge shall have the same meaning as set forth in O.C.G.A. § 12-5-30.3(a)(1), as may be amended from time to time.

As of its inclusion in this Ordinance, the term “sludge” means the solid or semisolid residue generated at a waste-water treatment or pretreatment plant. Such term specifically excludes treated effluent, septage, and sludge that has been treated to further reduce pathogens by such processes as composting, heat drying, or heat treating.

Soil amendment shall have the same meaning as set forth in 0.C.G.A. § 2-12-71(11), as may be amended from time to time.

As of its inclusion in this Ordinance, the term “soil amendment” means any substance intended for changing the characteristics of soil or other growth medium for the purposes of: increasing penetrability of water or air; increasing water-holding capacity; alleviating or decreasing soil compaction; or otherwise altering the soil or other medium in such manner that the physical properties are materially enhanced. The term “soil amendment’ does not include any substance for which nutritional claims are made, such as, but not limited to, commercial fertilizers, liming materials, or unmanipulated vegetable or animal manures. With respect to sewage sludge, the term “soil amendment’ will only include “exceptional quality sludge” and “Class A Sewage Sludge”, as those terms are defined and used in Ga. Comp. R. and Regs. 391-3-6-.17.

the Land Use Ordinance of the Code of Warren County Georgia, is hereby amended to add a definition for the term "nuisance" as follows:

Nuisance: This term shall have the same meaning as set forth in 0.C.G.A. § 41-1-1, as may be amended from time to time.

As of its inclusion in this Ordinance, “nuisance” means anything that causes hurt, inconvenience, or damage to another and the fact that the act done may otherwise be lawful shall not keep it from being a nuisance. The inconvenience complained of shall not be fanciful, or such as would affect only one of fastidious taste, but it shall be such as would affect an ordinary, reasonable man.

Use Ordinance of the Code of Warren County, Georgia, is hereby amended to include Section 5.9.5 ("Soil Amendments: Storage and Application”) to read as follows:

Any manufacture, storage, or application of soil amendments, as defined in Sec. 2.1, shall occur in compliance with all applicable state and federal laws and regulations, including the statutory requirements of the Georgia Soil Amendment Act (O.C.G.A. § 2-12-70 et. seq.) and applicable regulations of the Department of Agriculture (Georgia Rules and Regulations 40-31-1 et seq.) Soil amendments must be registered with the Commissioner of the Department of Agriculture and adhere to all applicable statutory provisions and regulations regarding their content, labeling, branding, application, use, and all other particulars.

10

This ordinance and its related definitions in Sec. 2.1 and 2.2 have adopted certain language found in the Georgia Soil Amendment Act and Department of Agriculture regulations. The purpose of this adoption is to prevent conflict between this ordinance and state law. This ordinance does not seek to supersede or infringe upon the authority of the Department of Agriculture in enforcing any statute or regulation, and it shall be interpreted in accordance with this intent. Any restrictions, and associated penalties, upon the location and timing of manufacturing, storing, transporting, applying, or using soil amendments within Warren County are subject to its authority per O.C.G.A. § 36-66-3 to pass zoning ordinances, as provided in 0.C.G.A. § 2-12-80(1)B) or elsewhere.

- (a) Manufacture, Storage, and Transporiation:

- (1) Storage of industrial waste and industrial byproducts as defined in Sec. 2.1 is permitted only in industrial districts.

- (2) Manufacture and processing of soil amendments derived from or including any industrial by-product are permitted only in industrial districts. Said manufacture and processing are expressly prohibited in any other district.

- (3) Storage of soil amendments containing or derived from industrial by-products for period exceeding twelve (12) hours is permitted only in industrial districts. To ensure compliance, the Administrator is authorized to examine the records of any industrial site (a) to or from which soil amendments have been transported; or (b) at which soil amendments have been stored or disposed.

- (4) Storage and transportation of soil amendments containing or derived from industrial by-products must be conducted in a manner which prevents all falling, leaking, spilling, or leaching, in accordance with Ga. Comp. R. & Regs. 40-31-1-.02(4)(b). Use of faulty storage devices or negligent transportation practices, regardless of whether an actual fall or leak has occurred, shall be deemed violations of this Ordinance.

Storage at the application property of soil amendments containing or derived from any industria! by-product must take place at least one-hundred (100) feet from any adjacent property line. This distance shall constitute a “buffer” within the meaning of 0.C.G.A. § 2-12-80(1)(B) of the Georgia Soil Amendment Act. This distance may increase as the Administrator deems necessary on a case-by-case basis to prevent harm to beneficial plants, animals, or aquatic life, pursuant to Ga. Comp. R. & Regs. 40-31-1-.02(3)(c).

- (b) Application and Use:

- (1) In accordance with the definition of soil amendments in Sec. 2.1, any application or use of soil amendments must be for a bona fide agricultural purpose rather than waste disposal. Disposal of industrial waste and by-products is restricted to industrial districts.

- (2) “Restricted districts” for purposes of this code section include any city and municipal parcels, office-institutional districts, residential districts (whether urban, suburban, or rural), the scenic corridor district, conservation districts, highway business districts,

11

and the interchange area commercial (IAC) district subject to the provisions of subsection (4).

- (3) “Water sources” for purposes of this code section includes the Ogeechee River Corridor (in addition to its inherent fifty (50) foot buffer per Sec. 7.1.3), all municipal water supply watersheds and reservoirs, public and private drinking water supply wells, other open wells, and sinkholes.

Any ponds or lakes located entirely within the property owned by the party seeking the permit to apply soil amendments are excepted from this provision. However, any easement, contract, or other agreement between the property owner and another party to use said pond or lake establishes the one-hundred (100) foot buffer, unless the other party waives the buffer in accordance with subsection (b\6).

Any state or federal regulations which impose a greater restriction or buffer shall supersede this ordinance.

- (4) Conditional use: Application and use of soil amendments containing industrial byproducts are permitted exclusively in forestry-agricultural districts. This use is subject to the following conditions. Any application or use must occur at least one-hundred (100) feet from (i) any adjacent property lines; (ii) any adjacent restricted districts listed in subsection (2); (iii) any adjacent residential property within a forestryagriculture district.; or (iv) any water sources as defined in subsection (3). Application and use are conditioned upon grant of a permit in accordance with subsection (5) , providing that the application is at least one-hundred (100) feet from any of the areas specified above. This distance shall constitute a “buffer” within the meaning of 0.C.G.A. § 2-12-80(1)(B) of the Georgia Soil Amendment Act, which buffer may increase as the Administrator deems necessary on a case-by-case basis to prevent harm to beneficial plants, animals, or aquatic life, as required by Ga. Comp. R. & Regs. 40-31-1-.02(3)(c).
30:
- (6) The buffer in Sec. 5.9.5(b)(4) may be waived by the owner(s) of residential property in a forestry-agriculture district via notarized, written consent filed with the Administrator. The consent shall include the name and signature(s) of the owner(s) giving their consent, the property address, the extent or distance of the waiver, the

date when such consent is given, and the length of time for which the owner(s) grant(s) their consent.

- (7) Subsurface injection as the only ;ermissible form of application: Application and use of soil amendments derived from an industrial by-product produced by a restaurant, kitchen, slaughterhouse, or food processing facility or from any industrial by-product which contains animal, fruit, or vegetable matter, liquid or otherwise, shall not be applied in any manner other than subsurface injection at a rate which leaves no significant amount of soil amendment on the soil's surface within one hour following injection, in accordance with Ga. Comp. R. & Regs. 40-31-1-.02(3)(b).

- (c) Nuisance

Any manufacture, storage, application, or use of soil amendments in violation of this ordinance shall constitute prime facie evidence of a nuisance. Nuisance may arise from a variety of factors, including but not limited to any one of the following.

- (1) Odor: any odor arising from the storage or application of soil amendments which inconveniences or damages any adjacent property owner while said owner is still within the confines of their property.

- (2) Pests: any pests (a) whose presence is attributable to the storage or application of soil amendments; and (b) who inconvenience or damage an adjacent property owner within the confines of their property. Damage may include personal injury or property damage to real estate, personal property, livestock, crops, or otherwise. Said pests shall include, but are not limited to, insects, reptiles, rodents, birds of prey, and all other vermin and carrion which may be attracted to the contents of the soil amendments in question.

- (3) Contamination: any contamination of the soil, water supply, air, crops, or livestock on adjacent property resulting from the storage or application of soil amendments.

The presence of any such a nuisance shall be grounds for immediate termination of a permit granted under subsection (b)(5). A nuisance may exist even when all other local and state laws have been followed.
